title: Microsoft Edge: opt-in for launching Edge when Windows starts on managed devices
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, policy behaviours and both configuration surfaces are supported. The full Group Policy route is documented across the two cited configuration pages, and the briefing correctly distinguishes the roadmap target from the controlled rollout already listed in release notes.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-11-20T23:20:27.
Microsoft plans an opt-in experience for users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches when Windows starts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge will introduce an opt-in experience that allows users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts.

claims.claim: The roadmap names LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled for administrative opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
claims.quote: Administrators can also manage this behavior through the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy with opt-in, opt-out, and user-choice configurations.

claims.quote: GP name: Launch Microsoft Edge on Windows startup; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge. Configure Microsoft Edge: open the Group Policy Editor and go to (Computer Configuration or User Configuration) > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The registry control is SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge, value LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled of type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled; Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, automatic launch is a user opt-in choice.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default. Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Both cited Stable releases describe autolaunch opt-in as a controlled feature rollout.
claims.quote: Note: This is a controlled feature rollout. If you don't see this change, check back as we continue the rollout.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: No fixed date is documented for the controlled rollout to reach a given tenant or all tenants.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner periodically frequency rollout completion date'; opened the policy and Stable release notes, and read archive and Beta excerpts. These give controlled rollout wording, not a tenant completion date.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence entitlement specific to autolaunch opt-in has been published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge for Business licensing requirements browser license pricing' and 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled licensing price meter cost'; opened the policy, Edge for Business, enterprise FAQ and management service. No autolaunch entitlement was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter for this feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled licensing price meter cost' and 'Microsoft Edge for Business license prerequisites pricing LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled autolaunch'; opened the policy, Edge for Business and enterprise FAQ, and read the roadmap. No autolaunch meter was stated.

claims.claim: No price for this feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled licensing price meter cost' and 'Microsoft Edge for Business FAQ license cost free requirements'; opened the policy, Edge for Business and enterprise FAQ, and read the roadmap. No autolaunch price was stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and policy page describe a launch setting, not new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge autolaunch opt-in managed devices data access automatic launch control policy'; read the roadmap and opened LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled. Both describe automatic visible launch and user choice without describing new data access.

claims.claim: For an unconfigured policy, the policy page describes the banner and user settings as the sources of an automatic-launch choice.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default. Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.claim: The documented administrative control for this item is LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled, configurable through Group Policy or the registry.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled Microsoft Edge management service admin center policy configure'; opened the policy, Windows policy configuration and management service pages. The feature-specific control found was LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled, with ADMX and registry settings.

claims.claim: The policy page documents no separate admin-centre switch for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled Microsoft Edge management service admin center policy configure'; opened the policy and management service pages. The policy page gives Group Policy and registry settings, not a separate admin-centre switch.

claims.claim: The policy page says the banner is shown periodically without specifying its frequency.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled opt-in banner periodically frequency rollout completion date'; opened the policy and Stable release notes. The policy says 'Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on' and gives no interval.
